name: Death at Ravenmoor Manor
caption: A Halloween murder mystery for 5–6 level 5 characters
description:
On All Hallows' Eve, Lord Silas Ravenmoor dies in a locked study minutes after the whole household sees the family ghost glide across the gallery. The party has until the midnight bell to prove the ghost was a man in a mask, and to unmask him.

A three-hour gothic mystery for the 2024 rules: a manor on three floors with walls, doors, lights and stairs between levels, six suspects, nineteen handouts and clue cards revealed one click at a time, the Twelve Candles clock, and one climactic fight in the chapel crypt.

Imports: the Ravenmoor Manor scene (three levels), 11 actors, 13 items, 5 journals and the Ravenmoor macros. Start with the Ravenmoor DM Guide journal.

biography.value:
Look. Family physician and amateur alchemist, 50s. Silver whiskers, half-moon spectacles, a voice like warm cocoa. Tonight: plague doctor costume, beaked mask stuffed with frost-mint and cloves, long oiled coat, tall buckled boots, mortar-and-pestle signet ring.

Wants. The manor, for the vein of moonsilver beneath the crypt. He secretly owns all of Edric's debts.

Tells. Smell of mint; foxfire paste under his fingernails (Perception DC 15); pond mud on his buckled boots; room dark at 8:45.

Plays as. Warm, grandfatherly, always 'just trying to help.' Steers suspicion to the ghost, then Edric, then Morwenna. In a zone of truth he goes quiet rather than lie.

Lines.

  • “Poor Silas. Fear is a terrible poison.”
  • “Edric owed a great deal of money. I only mention it because I care.”
  • “You lot were supposed to stay scared!”

Gear. Medical bag with a false bottom (holds the new will); Acid flasks; Scalpels; Snuffing powder; Plague doctor mask; Signet ring with a mortar and pestle.

The Chapel Crypt (midnight bell)

Quill fights in the chapel crypt beneath Ravenmoor Manor. On initiative count 20 (losing ties), as the midnight bell tolls, the crypt takes one lair action, in order.

  1. Round 1, The dead rise. Two Ravenmoor skeletons burst from coffins. If the party earned the Why Unmasking Edge, Edric and Bramwell hold the lids shut and nothing happens.
  2. Round 2, Candles gutter. A ghostly wail fills the crypt. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, each player character. Failure: the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.
  3. Round 3, Green flame. The brazier flares. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature within 10 feet of the brazier. Failure: 7 (2d6) Fire damage. From now on, if Quill starts his turn next to the brazier holding the will, he can burn it as a Bonus Action.
  4. Round 4, The Widow's due. Elspeth's spirit rises from her tomb (also triggers early when Quill drops below half his Hit Points). Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, Quill only. Failure: he has the Frightened condition until the fight ends.

description.value: Quill is immune to his own Banshee's Breath and has Advantage on saving throws against poison.

When Quill is reduced to 30 Hit Points or fewer (50 if the session is running long), he tears off his mask and surrenders. His skeletons crumble and his scarecrows slump lifeless.

biography.value:
Look. Silas's second wife, 40s. Sharp cheekbones, black-feathered swan mask and gown, a fan she snaps shut when annoyed. Stable mud on her hem.

Wants. Out of a cold marriage; to leave at dawn with a lover who signs his letters 'R.'

Secret. Her packed trunk is in a carriage in the stables and R.'s love letter (C12) is tucked in her glove. She spent 8:30-9:00 loading the carriage.

Knows. At about 8:45, from the stable yard, she saw a green glow moving past the chapel windows. Shares it once her secret is safe (Persuasion DC 14, or the letter plus a promise of discretion).

Plays as. Clipped and haughty; softens only when treated with respect.

Lines.

  • “I was in my room. With a headache. Which you are now giving me.”
  • “If I tell you what I saw, my business stays my own. Agreed?”

biography.value:
Look. Eldest son, 30s. Flushed face, black cloak with the collar hitched over his head, grinning papier-mache pumpkin head under one arm. Usually holding a glass.

Wants. His inheritance, to pay debts that terrify him. Underneath, his father's approval.

Secret. Ruinous gambling debts. Letter H3 in his coat says a new creditor bought them all; sealed in green wax with a mortar-and-pestle stamp. He spent 8:30-9:00 alone in the wine cellar (true).

Knows. Around 8:40 he heard footsteps and dripping behind the cellar's bricked-up arch. Goes pale when he learns Quill's signet ring bears a mortar and pestle. Quill frames him at candle 8.

Plays as. Bluster, self-pity and bad jokes.

Lines.

  • “I'd say I lost my head, but that's just the costume.”
  • “Father and I argued about money. We always argued about money. That's not murder, that's family.”

biography.value:
Look. Silas's granddaughter, 19, student illusionist. Ink-stained fingers, an enormous witch's hat that keeps sliding over her eyes. Talks fast, apologizes often, braver than she looks.

Wants. To know Elspeth, the grandmother she never met.

Secret. For a month she has used Minor Illusion to stage Widow sightings to make Silas talk about Elspeth (C13). She spent 8:30-9:00 changing out of an ink-stained costume (true).

Knows. Tonight's ghost was not hers: her illusions are just light, they don't snuff candles or leave smudges, and the lantern had real green glass. Detect Magic or Arcana DC 12 confirms no illusion on the gallery.

Plays as. Guilty, eager, natural ally. Quill attacks her at candle 4. If befriended she joins the showdown and hands out counter-herb sprigs (How Unmasking Edge).

Lines.

  • “Okay. So. The other ghosts were me. Not this one! This one was solid!”
  • “Grandfather took his tonic from the doctor every night...”

description.value: Pip knows whether any effect she can see within 30 feet is an illusion.
Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 120 ft. Hit: 5 (1d10) Fire damage.

Pip casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13): At Will: Light, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation. 2/Day Each: Disguise Self, Silent Image. 1/Day: Invisibility.

You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

A creature you touch has the &Reference[invisible apply=false] condition until the spell ends. The spell ends early immediately after the target makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.

description.value:
You make yourself—including your clothing, armor, weapons, and other belongings on your person—look different until the spell ends. You can seem 1 foot shorter or taller and can appear heavier or lighter. You must adopt a form that has the same basic arrangement of limbs as you have. Otherwise, the extent of the illusion is up to you.

The changes wrought by this spell fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, if you use this spell to add a hat to your outfit, objects pass through the hat, and anyone who touches it would feel nothing.

To discern that you are disguised, a creature must take the Study action to inspect your appearance and succeed on an [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC.

You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 15-foot Cube. The image appears at a spot within range and lasts for the duration. The image is purely visual; it isn't accompanied by sound, smell, or other sensory effects.

As a Magic action, you can cause the image to move to any spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image. For example, if you create an image of a creature and move it, you can alter the image so that it appears to be walking.

Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it. A creature that takes a Study action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.

biography.value:
Look. Groundskeeper and gravedigger, 60s. Stooped, mud to the knees, smells of pond water and pipe smoke. Scarecrow-patched coat, lantern, a shovel he never puts down.

Wants. Elspeth to rest in peace.

Secret. Every Hallows' Eve he lights warding lanterns around the pond; he was there 8:30-9:00. Decades ago he helped brick up part of an old passage under the house.

Knows. The passage runs from the chapel crypt up to the master's study, behind the bookshelves. Two scarecrows are missing (C9). Shares it if the party helps with his lanterns, respects the legend, or wins Insight/Persuasion DC 13.

Plays as. Gruff and slow, spits between sentences, lowers his voice at any mention of the pond. With the Why Edge he and Edric hold the coffin lids shut.

Lines.

  • “Mind the pond. She's restless tonight.”
  • “She walks every Hallows' Eve. Never hurt a soul. Not till now, they'll say. They'll be wrong.”

Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

biography.value:
Look. Housekeeper of forty years, 70s. Iron-grey bun, housekeeper's black, a ring of keys you hear two rooms away. She notices everything.

Wants. Elspeth remembered and the truth told.

Secret. She places white lilies (Elspeth's flower) in the study every Hallows' Eve; they were on the desk at 7:00. She never forgave Silas for the night Elspeth drowned.

Knows. The 'ghost' that brushed past her on the servants' stair at 8:57 wore men's buckled boots and smelled of mint. At 8:45 Quill's room was dark and empty. The doctor always adds 'his drops' himself. The tonic glass is unwashed in the scullery.

Plays as. Stern and precise; softens when anyone speaks kindly of Elspeth.

Lines.

  • “I've kept this house forty years. I know every footstep in it, and that ghost walked like a man.”
  • “The doctor always added his own drops. Always.”

description.value: Mrs. Crane carries keys to every lock in Ravenmoor Manor except Silas's lockbox.

biography.value:
Look. The family solicitor, a damp and nervous halfling. Fogged spectacles, dripping cloak, a satchel (holding the old will) clutched to his chest. Arrives at midnight by the ferry path.

Wants. To read the correct will, be paid, and go home to bed.

Knows. The old will leaves everything to Edric. Silas told him a new will existed but not its contents. A genuine Ravenmoor will bears Silas's black raven seal, so he can confirm the recovered will on sight.

Plays as. Fussy and easily startled, scrupulously honest. Reads whichever valid will is in front of him at midnight.

Lines.

  • “Fennick Barrowdown, solicitor. I'm here to read Lord Ravenmoor's will. Which will, I'm told, is... in question?”

Look. Elspeth Ravenmoor, Silas's first wife, drowned in the manor pond on All Hallows' Eve thirty years ago. Pale woman, grey gown, veil, lantern of green glass. Never speaks; only bows her head.

Appears. Exactly twice: rising from her tomb in round 4 of the showdown (or when Quill drops below half HP), and standing on the pond at dawn in the epilogue. Afterward her lantern waits on her memorial stone; it works as a Lantern of Revealing.

biography.value:
Look. Lord of Ravenmoor, 70s. Thin as a rake, velvet robe, raven-headed cane. Dry, dark humor; far more frightened than he lets on.

Wants. His new will read at midnight: the manor to Hollow Brook as an orphanage paid for with the moonsilver, as atonement for Elspeth.

Speak with dead (five questions).

  • Who killed you? “I saw no one. Only the cold. My tonic tasted of mint.”
  • Was it the ghost? “Elspeth would never harm me.”
  • Where is the will? “Gone from the box. I heard the bookcase groan before the dark.”
  • Who knew about the passage? “Hatch. Crane. And the doctor. I showed him myself when my legs failed.”
  • Anything else? “Under the chapel... silver. Let it build something good.”

Lines.

  • “If I'm dead before the bell, the old will stands, and that I will not allow.”
  • “Elspeth walks tonight, they say. She'll have to wait her turn.”
  • “It will disappoint everyone at dinner.”

Note. Alive only in Act 1. For Act 2, place a second token named 'Lord Silas Ravenmoor (body)' in his study chair with the Dead status.

text.content:
On All Hallows' Eve, @UUID[Actor.ju55ASDCcVhTtED0]{Lord Silas Ravenmoor} dies in a locked study minutes after the whole household sees the family ghost glide across the gallery. The party has until the midnight bell to prove the ghost was a man in a mask, and to unmask him.
Party 5–6 characters, level 5, mixed experience
Length One 3-hour session
Combat One climactic fight in the chapel crypt
Tone Gothic Halloween with a Saturday-morning-cartoon twist: spooky, a little silly, always solvable
Rules D&D 2024 rules (the newest edition), plus six house rules

The hook. Each character receives Silas's invitation (@UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.5gJy8OoqgMwwPOi8]{Handout 1}): 200 gp apiece to attend the Ravenmoor Hallows' Masque as guests and quiet bodyguards, because "someone under my roof wishes me dead before midnight." It is a costume party, so ask each player to describe their character's costume.

Bring to the table: 12 tealights or paper candle cards, a bag of wrapped candy (2 per player plus extras), the printed handouts, clue cards and DM screen.

The rest of the kit (in this module): the DM Guide journal for prep, rulings and what-ifs; the actors for stat blocks and roleplay profiles; the Handouts & Clues journal for every printable card, revealed to players one at a time; the Locations journal, linked from every map pin.

@UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Dr. Thaddeus Quill}, the kindly family physician, poisoned @UUID[Actor.ju55ASDCcVhTtED0]{Silas}, dressed as the Lantern Widow to blame the ghost, and stole the new will. If it stays lost, the old will hands the manor to @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric}, whose debts Quill secretly owns.

The legend. Thirty years ago Silas's first wife, Elspeth, drowned in the manor pond on All Hallows' Eve. Villagers say she returns every Hallows' Eve as the Lantern Widow, a veiled woman with a green lantern who claims one Ravenmoor life.

The motive. While treating Silas, Quill learned of a vein of moonsilver beneath the chapel crypt. He quietly bought up all of Edric's gambling debts. Under the old will Edric inherits the manor, and Quill would seize it to settle those debts. Silas's new will gives the manor to the village of Hollow Brook as an orphanage paid for by the moonsilver, with small stipends for family and staff. If the new will is read at midnight, Quill gets nothing.

The method.

  1. Poison. At the feast, Quill gave Silas his nightly heart tonic laced with Banshee's Breath, an alchemical poison. It acts in about 45 minutes, chills the skin and freezes the face in terror. It looks exactly like death by fright, and it smells faintly of mint.
  2. The locked room. Silas locked himself in his study at 8:25, as he always does. A forgotten passage runs from behind the study bookcase down to the chapel crypt. Quill came up it, found Silas dead, took the new will from its lockbox, splashed pond water from a flask and opened the window.
  3. The ghost. Back in the crypt, Quill put on a pale gown, a veil and gloves smeared with glowing foxfire fungus paste, and lit a green-glass lantern. He climbed the servants' stair to the minstrels' gallery, appeared above the Great Hall and blew out every candle with a pinch of alchemical snuffing powder.
  4. The cover. He stuffed the costume into an empty crypt niche, then hurried to the study with his medical bag and declared that Silas had been frightened to death.

Where the will is. In the false bottom of Quill's medical bag. He plans to burn it in the chapel's Hallows' brazier at midnight.

Every other suspect is hiding a secret that has nothing to do with the murder. Those secrets are the red herrings, and each one pays off with a clue that points back toward the truth.

These rules keep the clock visible, the party moving and the finale short, so the session lands on three hours. Explain rules 1–5 at the start; save rule 6 for the accusation.

  1. Twelve Candles. At 9:00 PM in-game, set 12 tealights or candle cards on the table. Every scene (searching a room, questioning a suspect, casting a ritual) snuffs one candle, which is 15 in-game minutes. When the last candle goes out, the midnight bell tolls and Act 3 begins, solved or not. If real time reaches 1:55, a sudden gust snuffs whatever candles remain.
  2. Split Up! The party may split into groups. While split, one scene for every group costs only one candle in total. Give each group about 5 real minutes, then cut away on a cliffhanger. It doubles the investigation speed and rewards the oldest mistake in horror.
  3. Clues Always Land. Core clues (marked ★) are never locked behind a roll. A failed check still finds the clue, but it costs an extra candle or triggers a jump scare. Rolls decide speed and bonus details, never whether the case can be solved.
  4. Treat Bag. Each player starts with 2 pieces of wrapped candy. Eat one to reroll a d20, to add 1d4 to a roll after seeing it, or to ask the DM one yes-or-no question about the case. Hand out more candy for great roleplay, sharp deductions and excellent screams.
  5. Scaredy-Cat Bonus. When a spooky moment calls for a Wisdom save, a player may fail on purpose and play it for laughs: shriek, dive into a suit of armor, leap into an ally's arms. They earn a candy. Outside combat, frightened from a scare ends at the end of the character's next turn.
  6. Unmask Him. At the accusation, the party must name who did it, how and why. Each correct answer grants one Unmasking Edge in the showdown (see Act 3). Skeletons die to any hit, and the fight ends when @UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Quill} drops to 30 hit points or fewer: he tears off his mask, surrenders, and his minions collapse.

Aim to finish the investigation by 1:55 so the accusation and fight get a full 50 minutes.

Act 1 has one job: show the players the study while @UUID[Actor.ju55ASDCcVhTtED0]{Silas} is alive, introduce all six suspects, then kill the lights. Keep each scene to about 6 minutes.

Scene 1: Arrival at dusk (6:30 PM)

Fog rolls off the moor and pools around the iron gates of Ravenmoor Manor. Jack-o'-lanterns line the long drive, each carved with a raven in flight, their candlelight flickering orange through the mist. A stooped man in a patched coat raises a lantern as you approach. "Guests, is it? Mind the pond," he grunts. "She's restless tonight."

@UUID[Actor.64tWZkvT3Aq5BPNj]{Bramwell Hatch}, the groundskeeper, leads them in. @UUID[Actor.bcnzHQSfDwEzt1u1]{Mrs. Crane}, the housekeeper, takes their coats and asks them to wait upon Lord Silas in his study.

Scene 2: The study (7:00 PM)

Lord Silas Ravenmoor is a thin old man wrapped in a velvet robe, leaning on a raven-headed cane. Behind him, a fire crackles beneath tall bookshelves. On his desk sits a small iron lockbox and a vase of white lilies.

Silas opens the lockbox to show a scroll sealed in black wax: his new will. "Master @UUID[Actor.gG0jEVDlvEP34M9J]{Fennick}, my solicitor, arrives at midnight to read it. If I'm dead before the bell, the old will stands, and that I will not allow." He won't say what the new will contains, only that "it will disappoint everyone at dinner." Asked about the legend, he chuckles: "Elspeth walks tonight, they say. She'll have to wait her turn."

Let the players poke around. What they see now matters later:

  • The window is latched from inside, and thick ivy grows undisturbed across the outer sill.
  • The lilies are already on the desk. Mrs. Crane put them there.
  • The lockbox key hangs on Silas's watch chain.
  • One bookcase stands slightly away from the wall (passive Perception 15 notices a cold draft).

Scene 3: The Hallows' feast (7:30 PM)

The Great Hall glows with a hundred candles. Paper bats hang from the rafters, and a roast boar steams on a table crowded with gourds and apples. Masked guests turn to look at you as you enter. Above, a dark minstrels' gallery overlooks the hall.

Introduce each suspect in one line, in costume (see The suspects): @UUID[Actor.KQKJNTGmT2yOlb2U]{Lady Morwenna} as a black swan, @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric} as a headless horseman, @UUID[Actor.QBfMKJlkNIfQacwd]{Pip} as a witch in an enormous hat, @UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Dr. Quill} as a plague doctor, Bramwell in his scarecrow coat, Mrs. Crane in housekeeper's black.

Plant three moments during the meal:

  • At 7:45, Quill takes a glass of tonic from Mrs. Crane's tray, turns his back to add "his drops" and hands it to Silas. Characters with passive Perception 16 or higher notice the turned back.
  • Edric and Silas argue loudly over money. Edric storms off to sulk.
  • At 8:25, Silas excuses himself to rest before midnight. Quill leaves at 8:30 "to fetch medicines from my room." Over the next few minutes, Morwenna, Pip and Bramwell drift away too.

When the party plays bodyguard. They were hired to protect Silas, so expect it:

  • Guarding the door: Silas refuses company in his study but lets them post a guard outside. That only deepens the locked-room puzzle, because no one passed the door.
  • Following Quill at 8:30: he heads for the guest wing, waits in the dark, then slips down the servants' stair. Let the follower lose him without a roll, but reward the effort: they know he never lit a candle in his room.
  • Detecting poison at dinner: let a sharp player catch it. Banshee's Breath shrugs off ordinary cures, and Silas insists on resting alone in his study anyway, so he still dies at 8:35. The party simply starts Act 2 already suspecting the tonic.

Scene 4: The Lantern Widow (8:55 PM)

A cold wind sweeps through the hall. One by one, the candles gutter. High on the minstrels' gallery, a green light blooms. A veiled woman in a pale gown stands there, a green lantern raised in one hand, glowing faintly from within. She lifts a single finger toward the family portraits. Then a gust howls across the hall and every candle dies at once.

In the dark, a scream rings out from the servants' stair (Mrs. Crane). Have everyone make a DC 13 Wisdom save against fright, and remind players of the Scaredy-Cat Bonus. By the time anyone reaches the gallery, it is empty.

Scene 5: The body (9:00 PM)

The study door is locked from inside. When the party breaks it down (or Bramwell does with his shovel):

Silas sits rigid in his chair, eyes wide, mouth open in a silent scream. Frost glitters on his fingertips. The window hangs open to the night, and wet footprints trail across the rug from the sill to the desk. The lockbox stands open and empty, and its key is gone from Silas's watch chain. White lilies lie scattered across the floor.

Dr. Quill pushes through moments later, medical bag in hand. After a quick examination he announces: "His heart gave out. He was frightened to death. The Widow has claimed her Ravenmoor." Morwenna, shaking, points out the obvious: the storm has flooded the road, no one can leave, and Fennick arrives at midnight. Without the new will, the old one stands.

Hand the players the suspect list (@UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.9jbFA2FdP6pWMkof]{Handout 2}), light the twelve candles, and start Act 2.

Five suspects look guilty and are hiding something harmless; the sixth, @UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Dr. Quill}, looks like the most helpful person in the house. Each innocent suspect gives up a ★ clue once their secret is out or respected.

Lady Morwenna Ravenmoor

@UUID[Actor.ju55ASDCcVhTtED0]{Silas}'s second wife, 40s. Costume: a black swan.

  • Looks guilty because: she was cut from the new will, was cold to Silas all evening, and her hem is caked with mud.
  • Secret: she plans to leave Silas at dawn. Her packed trunk sits in a carriage in the stables, and a love letter signed "R." is tucked in her glove.
  • Claimed alibi: "In my room with a headache." Truth: loading the carriage in the stables.
  • ★ Reveals (Persuasion DC 14, or if the party finds the letter and promises discretion): from the stable yard at about 8:45, she saw a green glow moving past the chapel windows, ten minutes before the ghost appeared in the hall.
  • Play her: clipped and haughty, fanning herself; she softens if treated with respect.

Edric Ravenmoor

Eldest son, 30s. Costume: a headless horseman, carrying his papier-mâché head under one arm.

  • Looks guilty because: he inherits everything under the old will, argued with Silas at dinner, and has been drinking steadily.
  • Secret: ruinous gambling debts. In his coat is a letter (@UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.fsJioYgjBt4PoLBz]{Handout 3}) saying his debts have been bought by a new creditor who expects payment the day he inherits. ★ It is sealed in green wax stamped with a mortar and pestle.
  • Claimed alibi: alone in the wine cellar, drinking. This is true.
  • ★ Reveals: at about 8:40 he heard footsteps and dripping water behind the cellar's old bricked-up arch, which backs onto the crypt. He has no idea who bought his debts, and goes pale when he learns that Quill's signet ring bears a mortar and pestle.
  • Play him: bluster, self-pity and bad jokes about losing his head.

Penelope "Pip" Ravenmoor

Granddaughter, 19, a student illusionist. Costume: a witch with an enormous hat.

  • Looks guilty because: servants gossip that the Widow has been seen all month, and @UUID[Actor.QBfMKJlkNIfQacwd]{Pip}'s spell notes in her room include sketches of a veiled lady with a lantern.
  • Secret: for a month she has used minor illusion to stage Widow sightings, hoping to get her grandfather to finally talk about Elspeth, the grandmother she never knew. She is terrified, because tonight's ghost was not hers.
  • Claimed alibi: changing out of an ink-stained costume in her room. This is true.
  • ★ Reveals: "My illusions are just light. They don't put out candles, and they don't leave smudges. That ghost was solid, and its lantern had green glass in it." With a detect magic or an Arcana check (DC 12), she confirms there is no lingering illusion on the gallery.
  • Play her: talks too fast, guilty and eager; she makes a good ally. If the party befriends her, she fights beside them in the showdown (see her actor sheet).

Dr. Thaddeus Quill (the killer)

Family physician and amateur alchemist, 50s. Costume: a plague doctor, with a beaked mask stuffed with herbs and tall buckled boots.

  • His story: "Silas's heart failed from fright." He volunteers to help, steering the party first toward the ghost, then toward @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric}'s debts, then toward @UUID[Actor.KQKJNTGmT2yOlb2U]{Morwenna}.
  • His lie: "I went to my room to fetch my medicines." But @UUID[Actor.bcnzHQSfDwEzt1u1]{Mrs. Crane} found his room dark and empty at 8:45, and characters who watched the feast may recall his bag never left his side.
  • Tells: he smells of frost-mint, the same smell as the poison. Glowing foxfire paste is caught under his fingernails (Perception DC 15 on a handshake or a close look). His buckled boots are wet with pond mud. His signet ring bears a mortar and pestle.
  • ★ Carries: the stolen new will, hidden in a false bottom of his medical bag (Investigation DC 15, or found automatically if he is searched after the accusation).
  • Under pressure: he leans on his medical authority, then blames Edric. Inside a zone of truth he goes quiet and speaks only in careful half-truths. A man who refuses to answer is a clue.
  • Play him: warm, grandfatherly and always "just trying to help." A little too helpful.

Bramwell Hatch

Groundskeeper and gravedigger, 60s. Costume: none, just his scarecrow-patched coat.

  • Looks guilty because: muddy boots, the smell of pond water, a shovel always in hand, and he mutters about the Widow constantly.
  • Secret: every Hallows' Eve he lights warding lanterns around the pond to keep Elspeth at rest. He was there from 8:30 to 9:00. Decades ago he helped brick up part of an old passage under the house.
  • ★ Reveals (Insight or Persuasion DC 13, or if the party helps relight his lanterns or treats the legend with respect): a hidden passage runs from the chapel crypt up to the master's study, behind the bookshelves. He also mentions that two of his scarecrows have gone missing from the pumpkin patch.
  • Play him: gruff and slow, tells the legend with relish and lowers his voice whenever the pond is mentioned.

Mrs. Agatha Crane

Housekeeper, 70s, in housekeeper's black, keys at her belt.

  • Looks guilty because: she was devoted to Elspeth and never forgave Silas for her death, and the scattered white lilies, Elspeth's flower, look like a ghost's calling card.
  • Secret: she places white lilies in the study every Hallows' Eve in Elspeth's memory. The party saw them there at 7:00.
  • Alibi: serving the feast, then on the servants' stair at 8:57 when the ghost brushed past her.
  • ★ Reveals: the "ghost" wore men's buckled boots and smelled of mint. When she turned down the beds at 8:45, Dr. Quill's room was dark and empty. She prepares the tonic tray, but the doctor always adds his own drops. The tonic glass is still unwashed in the scullery.
  • Play her: stern and precise; she softens when anyone speaks kindly of Elspeth.

Study (the crime scene)

  • ★ The bookcase: a pale scuff arc on the floorboards and a cold draft. Pulling Hallowed Rites of the Ravenmoor Line swings the case open (Investigation DC 14, or passive Perception 15).
  • Missing key: the lockbox key is gone from @UUID[Actor.ju55ASDCcVhTtED0]{Silas}'s watch chain. Whoever opened the box took it, and Quill plants it in @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric}'s coat at candle 8.
  • Red herring: the scattered lilies (@UUID[Actor.bcnzHQSfDwEzt1u1]{Mrs. Crane}'s).

  • ★ Fresh candle wax on the steps, green glowing smudges on the walls, and a dropped sprig of frost-mint.

Minstrels' gallery

  • ★ Glowing green smears on the railing. Nature DC 12 identifies foxfire, a glowing fungus paste, not magic.
  • Detect magic shows no magic at all: no illusion, no necromancy. Whatever snuffed the candles was not a spell.

Servants' stair

  • ★ A muddy print of a buckled boot on one step, and drips of pond water leading down toward the chapel corridor.

Chapel and crypt

  • ★ The costume: in an empty wall niche behind Elspeth's tomb, a bundle holding a pale gown, a veil, gloves crusted with foxfire paste, a green-glass lantern and a flask of pond water (Investigation DC 13).
  • ★ Moonsilver: a silver-blue glint in a crack in the crypt floor (Arcana or Nature DC 14). Someone has been chipping at it.
  • Two pumpkin-headed scarecrows stand oddly in the corner, and a chalk circle is half-hidden under a tarp. Quill has prepared for trouble; this foreshadows the finale.

Scullery

  • ★ Silas's unwashed tonic glass. The residue is frosted and smells of mint. Medicine or alchemist's supplies DC 13 identifies Banshee's Breath.

Dr. Quill's guest room

  • The bed is still unturned, and the fireplace has been cold all night.
  • ★ An alchemy notebook (@UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.fIUcA6ktUrArCZ7C]{Handout 4}) with a recipe for Banshee's Breath (Investigation DC 13).
  • A stick of green sealing wax that matches the seal on Edric's debt letter.

Library

  • ★ Silas's journal (@UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.nWfZK1SRR6PG0ZmP]{Handout 5}): his last entry notes that Quill keeps asking about the crypt.
  • A portrait of Elspeth holding a lantern, its glass painted green.

Wine cellar

Stables

  • Red herring: @UUID[Actor.KQKJNTGmT2yOlb2U]{Morwenna}'s carriage, packed trunk and a love letter from "R."

  • @UUID[Actor.64tWZkvT3Aq5BPNj]{Bramwell}'s warding lanterns and Elspeth's memorial stone.

Running each candle

Ask the party where they go and who they talk to, run the scene, then snuff a candle. Answer questions generously. When players chase a red herring, let it pay off: every innocent suspect's secret leads to a ★ clue that points somewhere else. If the table goes quiet, have Dr. Quill wander in to "help" and drop a confident wrong theory. Players love proving him wrong.

If the party cracks it early. If they find the will in Quill's bag before midnight, he smashes a smoke flask, snatches it back and bolts for the crypt. Skip the accusation, grant the Who Unmasking Edge plus any How or Why they can state on the spot, and spend the saved time on the epilogue.

Spells the party may use

Rulings for other spells and abilities, including detect poison and disease, locate object and augury, are in the DM Guide journal.

  • Speak with dead on Silas (five questions, answered in a frightened whisper):

    • Who killed you? "I saw no one. Only the cold. My tonic tasted of mint."
    • Was it the ghost? "Elspeth would never harm me."
    • Where is the will? "Gone from the box. I heard the bookcase groan before the dark."
    • Who knew about the passage? "Hatch. Crane. And the doctor. I showed him myself when my legs failed."
    • Anything else? "Under the chapel... silver. Let it build something good."

  • Detect magic: reveals no magic at all anywhere the ghost appeared. The chalk circle in the crypt glows with necromancy.

  • Zone of truth or detect thoughts: the innocents give up their secrets. Quill dodges, goes silent, or blurts something about the crypt.

Escalations

  • Candle 4: The Widow strikes again. A crash in the library. Pip is found dazed on the floor, her spell notes gone, the air smelling of mint. She says the veiled ghost shoved her and whispered, "Stop meddling." If the party checks, Quill was "resting in his room" once again, and his room is still dark. Quill is silencing the one witness who can prove the ghost was not magic. Run this only while Quill is out of the party's sight; if he has stuck by them all night, he slipped away during the last scene change, so ask who was watching him.
  • Candle 8: A convenient culprit. Quill calls everyone to the Great Hall. The lockbox key has turned up in Edric's coat, and Quill gravely accuses him. Edric is drunk and furious. The party can see that Quill handled the coat last (Insight DC 13 senses he is performing). Planted evidence that conveniently solves everything is its own clue.
  • Candle 11: The bell tower creaks. Lights from @UUID[Actor.gG0jEVDlvEP34M9J]{Fennick}'s carriage appear on the drive. Quill excuses himself "to say a prayer for Silas in the chapel." He is off to light the brazier.

If the party is stuck

Climb this ladder, one rung per stalled candle:

  1. A suspect remembers something: Mrs. Crane mentions the boots, or Bramwell mentions his missing scarecrows.
  2. A player eats a candy to ask a yes-or-no question (house rule 4).
  3. A spooky nudge: the study bookcase creaks open by itself in a cold draft, or green light flickers in the chapel window.
  4. Pip pieces it together aloud: "Grandfather took his tonic from the doctor every night..."

At midnight the party names who, how and why in the Great Hall; whatever they say, @UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Quill} bolts for the chapel crypt and the session ends in one fight there.

The accusation (15 minutes)

The bell in the tower tolls twelve. The doors swing open and a damp, nervous halfling in a dripping cloak hurries in, clutching a satchel. "@UUID[Actor.gG0jEVDlvEP34M9J]{Fennick Barrowdown}, solicitor. I'm here to read Lord Ravenmoor's will. Which will, I'm told, is... in question?"

Gather every suspect and let the party make their case. Ask them to name who, how and why (house rule 6), then award Unmasking Edges:

They name correctly Unmasking Edge
Who: Dr. Quill No surprise for Quill. Every character rolls initiative with advantage.
How: poisoned tonic, plus the passage or the costume @UUID[Actor.QBfMKJlkNIfQacwd]{Pip} hands out sprigs of counter-herb. Every character has advantage on saves against Banshee's Breath.
Why: @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric}'s debts, the moonsilver or the stolen will Edric and @UUID[Actor.64tWZkvT3Aq5BPNj]{Bramwell} rush in behind the party and hold the coffin lids shut. The round 1 lair action does nothing.

If they accuse Quill, he laughs softly, smashes a smoke flask on the flagstones and flees for the chapel crypt. If they accuse someone else, Quill nods gravely, "Then justice is done," and slips away. @UUID[Actor.bcnzHQSfDwEzt1u1]{Mrs. Crane} or Pip notices a minute later and raises the alarm. Either way, the party catches him in the crypt with the will in one hand, inches from the lit brazier.

The showdown (35 minutes)

Green fire roars in the brazier. Dr. Quill stands inside a chalk circle, his beaked mask gleaming, the will held over the flames. "Ravenmoor's dead belong to me tonight." Coffin lids grind open. In the corner, two scarecrows lift their carved pumpkin heads, candlelight blazing behind their grins.

The crypt: about 50 by 40 feet, dim light. Stone coffins give half cover. Two iron candelabras can be knocked over (an action) to set a 10-foot square ablaze for 2d6 fire damage to anything inside. The scarecrows hate that. The brazier sits at the far end. The fire is not hot enough to take the will until the round 3 flare. From then on, if Quill starts his turn next to it holding the will, he can drop it in as a bonus action. A character next to Quill can snatch the will with an action and a contested Athletics or Sleight of Hand check.

Enemies:

Party size Dr. Quill Pumpkin-headed scarecrows Skeletons
5 characters 162 Hit Points 1 4
6 characters 162 Hit Points 2 4

Under the 2024 rules this is a Moderate encounter: 4,400 XP for six characters (4,450 once the two lair skeletons join), and 3,700 for five (3,750 with them).

If the clock runs past 2:35 in real time, Quill surrenders at 50 hit points instead of 30. Run all the skeletons on one initiative count to keep rounds quick.

Lair actions (initiative count 20, as the midnight bell keeps tolling):

  1. Round 1, The dead rise: two more skeletons burst from coffins.
  2. Round 2, Candles gutter: a ghostly wail. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, each player character. Failure: the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. The Scaredy-Cat Bonus applies.
  3. Round 3, Green flame: the brazier flares. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature within 10 feet of it. Failure: 7 (2d6) Fire damage.
  4. Round 4, or as soon as Quill drops below half his Hit Points, The Widow's due: a cold green light rises from Elspeth's tomb, and a veiled shape stands in it. It is not Pip, and it is not a costume. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, Quill only. Failure: he has the Frightened condition until the fight ends.

Dr. Thaddeus Quill

Medium Humanoid, Neutral Evil

  • AC 15 (oiled leather coat) · Initiative +3 (13) · HP 162 (25d8 + 50); surrenders at 30 · Speed 30 ft.
  • STR 10 (+0) · DEX 16 (+3) · CON 14 (+2) · INT 18 (+4) · WIS 13 (+1) · CHA 14 (+2)
  • Saving Throws Dex +6, Int +7, Wis +4 · Skills Deception +5, Medicine +7 · Senses Passive Perception 11 · Languages Common, Elvish · CR 7 (XP 2,900; PB +3)
  • Plague Mask. Quill is immune to his own Banshee's Breath and has Advantage on saving throws against poison.
  • Multiattack. Quill makes three attacks, using Scalpel or Acid Flask in any combination.
  • Scalpel. Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.
  • Acid Flask. Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 30/60 ft. Hit: 10 (3d6) Acid damage.
  • Banshee's Breath (Recharge 5–6). Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 22 (5d8) Poison damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.
  • Ring the Bone Bell (Bonus Action). Up to two allies Quill can see move up to half their Speed, and one of them makes one attack.
  • Snuffing Powder (Bonus Action, 2/Day). Quill flings alchemical powder at a point within 60 feet. Every nonmagical flame in a 20-foot-radius Sphere there goes out in a cold rush of air.
  • Slippery Physician (Reaction). Trigger: A melee attack roll hits Quill. Response: He adds 3 to his AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss. If it misses, he moves up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Pumpkin-headed scarecrow

Medium Construct, Unaligned

  • AC 13 · Initiative +2 (12) · HP 52 (8d8 + 16) · Speed 30 ft.
  • STR 16 (+3) · DEX 14 (+2) · CON 14 (+2) · INT 4 (−3) · WIS 10 (+0) · CHA 1 (−5)
  • Vulnerabilities Fire · Immunities Poison; Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned · Senses Darkvision 60 ft., Passive Perception 10 · CR 3 (XP 700; PB +2)
  • False Appearance. While motionless, it looks like an ordinary scarecrow.
  • Pumpkin Burst. When it drops to 0 Hit Points, its carved head bursts in candle flame. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature within 5 feet. Failure: 10 (3d6) Fire damage.
  • Multiattack. The scarecrow makes two Claw attacks.
  • Claw. Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage.
  • Grinning Glare (Recharge 5–6). Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature within 30 feet that can see the scarecrow. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn, and its Speed is 0 while Frightened this way.

Skeleton (minion)

Medium Undead, Lawful Evil

  • AC 13 · Initiative +2 (12) · HP destroyed by any damage · Speed 30 ft. · CR 1/8 (XP 25)
  • Shortsword. Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage.
  • Shortbow. Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 80/320 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage.

The unmasking

When Quill drops to 30 hit points or fewer, the skeletons collapse into dust, the scarecrows slump, and he tears off his beaked mask.

"Thirty years I bandaged this wretched family's wounds, and I'd have owned every stone of this house by morning. You lot were supposed to stay scared!"

The ending turns on two things: whether the party caught @UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Quill}, and whether the new will survived the brazier. @UUID[Actor.gG0jEVDlvEP34M9J]{Fennick} pays the party's fee from the estate, and how much depends on the outcome.

Outcome What happens Reward per character
Quill caught, will saved Fennick reads the new will in the Great Hall. The manor becomes the Hollow Brook orphanage, the moonsilver pays for it, and every family member and servant gets a modest stipend. Quill waits in the cellar for the dawn constable. 200 gp, plus the lantern below
Quill caught, will burned The old will stands and @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric} inherits. Shaken and sober, he swears before witnesses to honor his father's wishes. Whether he keeps that promise is a hook for another night. 150 gp
Quill escapes He vanishes through the pond fog with the will's ashes and a grudge. The party has made a recurring villain. 100 gp

The new will holds one last line for the party: "To whoever unmasks my killer, should it come to that: my cane, and my thanks." The raven-headed cane is a fine walking stick worth 50 gp.

The real ghost

End every version of the night with this:

As you step out into the grey before dawn, @UUID[Actor.64tWZkvT3Aq5BPNj]{Bramwell}'s warding lanterns around the pond flicker, one by one, from orange to green. On the still water stands a pale woman in a veil, holding a lantern of green glass. She bows her head to you, once. Then the fog closes, and she is gone.

On Elspeth's memorial stone, the party finds her old green-glass lantern, dry and warm. It works as a lantern of revealing. Was the Widow real? Let the players argue about it on the way home.

Show Handouts 1 and 2 to every player; reveal 3, 4 and 5 only when the party finds them. How: he poisoned @UUID[Actor.ju55ASDCcVhTtED0]{Silas}'s 7:45 tonic with Banshee's Breath, used the secret passage to enter the locked study and steal the new will, then played the Lantern Widow in a gown, veil and glowing foxfire gloves. The will is in the false bottom of Quill's medical bag. Every other suspect is guilty of something harmless: @UUID[Actor.KQKJNTGmT2yOlb2U]{Morwenna} is eloping, Edric is broke, @UUID[Actor.QBfMKJlkNIfQacwd]{Pip} faked earlier ghosts, @UUID[Actor.64tWZkvT3Aq5BPNj]{Bramwell} keeps ghost-warding rituals, and @UUID[Actor.bcnzHQSfDwEzt1u1]{Mrs. Crane} left the lilies.

About two hours of prep in total, most of it a week out.

A week before

  • ☐ Read the Adventure journal once, start to finish

  • ☐ Order or pick up props, especially the plague doctor mask
  • ☐ Ask players to bring level 5 characters and think up a costume for them

The day before

  • ☐ Print any paper handouts and the DM screen you want at the table
  • ☐ Seal the will scroll and @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric}'s letter (if using physical props)
  • ☐ Read Act 1 aloud once to find your pace, and practice Quill's voice
  • ☐ Open the crypt and check the showdown tokens and the Midnight Bell lair actions

Thirty minutes before

  • ☐ Set up the DM screen with the solution panel facing you
  • ☐ Lay out the twelve tealights (or open the Twelve Candles clock), candy, and the doctor's bag by your seat
  • ☐ Cue the ambience playlist

pages.name: If the players do this, you do that

text.content:
Whatever the players try, keep the case solvable and the clock moving; never block a good idea, just make it cost a candle.

If the players... You...
Accuse someone before candle 6 Let @UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Quill} agree warmly. Run the next escalation while the accused is under guard, which proves them wrong.
Want to search Quill or his bag He refuses indignantly: "Patient records, sir!" A forced search or Sleight of Hand (DC 15) finds the will, and the finale starts early (Adventure, Act 2).
Try to leave or send for help The road is flooded and the ferry won't cross until @UUID[Actor.gG0jEVDlvEP34M9J]{Fennick} does at midnight. @UUID[Actor.64tWZkvT3Aq5BPNj]{Bramwell} warns them off the pond path.
Attack or threaten a suspect Bramwell steps in with his shovel and the household goes cold. The frightened suspect blurts out their secret, not a confession.
Fixate on one innocent suspect Let the evidence fail to stick. Have that suspect volunteer their ★ clue, which points somewhere else.
Watch Quill all night He slips away during a scene change. If they truly never let him go, he bolts with a smoke flask at the midnight bell.
Split into many groups One candle per round of scenes, about 5 real minutes per group, and cut away on cliffhangers.
Run long Merge Escalations 2 and 3, have @UUID[Actor.QBfMKJlkNIfQacwd]{Pip} piece it together aloud, and snuff two candles per scene.
Finish early Stretch the epilogue: Fennick reads every bequest, and the party can explore the moonsilver in the crypt.
Leave one player quiet Give them an NPC who will only confide in them. Pip picks the shyest character.

pages.name: Rulings for investigation spells and abilities

text.content:
Level 5 characters have real tools; let them work, because a clue that lands fast leaves more time for the fun parts.

Spell or ability What it reveals
Detect magic No magic at all where the ghost appeared. The chalk circle and the two scarecrows in the crypt glow with necromancy.
Detect poison and disease Poison in @UUID[Actor.ju55ASDCcVhTtED0]{Silas}'s body, residue in the tonic glass (@UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.go44g73lk20faCfw]{C6}), and a faint trace inside @UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Quill}'s bag, where an empty vial rolls loose.
Speak with dead Silas's five answers (Adventure, Act 2).
Zone of truth Innocent suspects give up their secrets. Quill goes silent or speaks only in careful half-truths.
Detect thoughts Surface thoughts: each suspect is fixated on their own secret. Quill is thinking "midnight... the brazier... don't look at the bag." Probing deeper, Quill makes a DC 13 Wisdom save (+4).
Locate object If the caster saw the will in Scene 2, it points to Quill's bag. Let it work; the finale starts early.
Augury "Search the doctor's bag": weal. "Accuse @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric}": woe.
Revivify Too late. Silas has been dead far longer than a minute.
Divine Sense Senses desecrated ground at the crypt's chalk circle.
Familiar or invisibility to tail someone Whoever they follow does exactly what the timeline says. Quill heads for the chapel at candle 11.
Insight against Quill Contest it with his Deception (+5). On a win: "He's hiding something, and he's very good at it."

The twist lands when players suspect @UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{Quill} late and then realize every clue was in plain sight. Five habits get you there:

  1. Make him useful. Quill offers real help: he confirms the poison once someone else finds it, and he patches up wounds. Players rarely suspect the NPC who keeps helping them.
  2. Give every suspect equal time. If you linger on Quill, players notice. Rotate the spotlight evenly through all six.
  3. Let him be wrong out loud. His theories about the ghost, then @UUID[Actor.qfcAVG1nR1fJKOuv]{Edric}, then @UUID[Actor.KQKJNTGmT2yOlb2U]{Morwenna} should be plausible and confident. Players enjoy proving the doctor wrong, and it hides that he is steering them.
  4. Never lie about a clue. Describe the mint smell, the buckled boots and the dark guest room plainly every time. Fairness is what makes the reveal satisfying.
  5. Save the mask. Keep the plague doctor mask out of sight until the showdown, then put it on. Pull it off at the unmasking for the big moment. (In Foundry: Quill's token stays masked until the Unmask macro swaps it.)

One hook per character is enough to keep six suspects distinct.

The easiest way to run the night is the Ravenmoor Director (macro, or Shift+R): one window with every set piece below in running order, ticks for what has already happened, and the state of the night (candles, clues, edges, session time). Its Set up my hotbar button puts the suggested macros in the slots below.

Every set piece is also a macro in the Ravenmoor macro folder. Each macro is one line that calls game.modules.get("ravenmoor-manor").api, so the logic updates with the module.

Also handy: double-click any read-aloud box in these journals to post it to chat for the players. Snuffing a candle can be bound to a key in Configure Controls. Reset the Night puts the map, NPCs and handouts back to the start, for a test run or a replay.

Ravenmoor SettingsParty size, running long, session start time and sound cues.

Running order

  1. Before the session: assign each player their character (User Configuration), then in the Director: Party arrives at the drive, Treat Bag (2 candy each), and Settings for the party size and, if you like, the session clock and sound cues.
  2. Act 1: Silas Retires (8:25), Lights Out (8:55), The Body (9:00). The Body lights the twelve candles and starts Act 2.
  3. Act 2: click a candle on the Twelve Candles panel after each scene. Reveal Handout whenever a card is found; the Clue Tracker ticks itself.
  4. Act 3: the twelfth candle runs Midnight and opens the Accusation. Then Showdown Setup, which builds the combat and the Midnight Bell lair turn.
  5. Epilogue: Unmask Quill fires on its own at his surrender threshold. Finish with Epilogue.

Every feature stands alone: if you prefer real tealights and candy, ignore the panels and nothing else breaks.

text.content:
Fog rolls off the moor and pools around the iron gates of Ravenmoor Manor. Jack-o'-lanterns line the long drive, each carved with a raven in flight, their candlelight flickering orange through the mist. A stooped man in a patched coat raises a lantern as you approach. "Guests, is it? Mind the pond," he grunts. "She's restless tonight."

  • Act 1, Scene 1 (6:30 PM). Bramwell Hatch meets the party with a lantern and leads them in.
  • At candle 11, the lights of Fennick's carriage appear here.

People: @UUID[Actor.64tWZkvT3Aq5BPNj]{Bramwell Hatch}

The road beyond the gates is flooded; no one can leave or send for help until Fennick crosses at midnight.

A black-and-white marble floor, two suits of armor flanking the inner doors, and a fat carved pumpkin grinning from a table draped in red.

  • Mrs. Crane takes the party's coats and asks them to wait upon Lord Silas in his study (doc, Scene 1).
  • At midnight Fennick arrives here, dripping, and is shown through to the Great Hall.

People: @UUID[Actor.bcnzHQSfDwEzt1u1]{Mrs. Agatha Crane}

The Great Hall glows with a hundred candles. Paper bats hang from the rafters, and a roast boar steams on a table crowded with gourds and apples. Masked guests turn to look at you as you enter. Above, a dark minstrels' gallery overlooks the hall.

Scene 4: The Lantern Widow (8:55 PM)

A cold wind sweeps through the hall. One by one, the candles gutter. High on the minstrels' gallery, a green light blooms. A veiled woman in a pale gown stands there, a green lantern raised in one hand, glowing faintly from within. She lifts a single finger toward the family portraits. Then a gust howls across the hall and every candle dies at once.

  • Act 1, Scene 3 (7:30 PM): the Hallows' feast. Introduce each suspect in one line, in costume.
  • 7:45: Quill takes a glass of tonic from Mrs. Crane's tray, turns his back to add "his drops" and hands it to Silas. Passive Perception 16+ notices the turned back.
  • Edric and Silas argue loudly over money; Edric storms off.
  • 8:25: Silas retires to his study. 8:30: Quill leaves "to fetch medicines from my room"; Morwenna, Pip and Bramwell drift away.
  • Act 1, Scene 4 (8:55 PM): the Widow appears on the gallery and every candle dies (Lights Out macro). A scream from the servants' stair (Mrs. Crane). Everyone makes a DC 13 Wisdom save against fright; remind players of the Scaredy-Cat Bonus.
  • Candle 8: Quill gathers everyone here and accuses Edric with the planted lockbox key.
  • Midnight: the accusation (Act 3).

The candelabras and the hall fire are in light group 'hall_candles'.

Two centuries of Ravenmoors stare down from gilt frames along a red runner. A suit of armor stands guard at each end, visor down, as if listening.

  • The family portraits the Widow pointed toward hang here. Nothing is hidden behind them; the gesture was theater.
  • A fine place for a Scaredy-Cat moment: diving into a suit of armor.

• Old floor plans that show the passage from crypt to study (History or Investigation DC 13).
  • ★ Silas's journal (Handout 5): his last entry notes that Quill keeps asking about the crypt.
  • A portrait of Elspeth holding a lantern, its glass painted green.
  • Candle 4 escalation: a crash in the library. Pip is found dazed on the floor, her spell notes gone, the air smelling of mint.

Run the candle 4 escalation only while Quill is out of the party's sight.

A broad oak stair climbs into shadow. Every third step creaks, and the house seems to hold its breath between them.

  • The main stair to the upper landing (level change region).

A low fire, two velvet sofas and a card table abandoned mid-game. It is the warmest room in the house and the only quiet one.

  • A natural place to question a suspect privately. Use it to rotate the spotlight evenly through all six.

Ledgers in perfect rows, a board of labeled hooks for the household keys, and a single candle burned exactly halfway down.

  • Every hook on the key board is filled. Mrs. Crane holds keys to every lock in the house except Silas's lockbox.
  • Supporting detail: a card in her neat hand reads "Heart tonic: hawthorn, honey, water. The doctor adds his own drops."

People: @UUID[Actor.bcnzHQSfDwEzt1u1]{Mrs. Agatha Crane}

Supports Mrs. Crane's testimony; not a numbered clue.

Copper pots, a banked hearth and the bones of the roast boar. Stone steps in the corner lead down into cold dark.

  • Stairs down to the wine cellar (level change region).
  • The hidden stair runs inside the thick east wall here. There is no opening on this floor.

Map pins on this page: 17. Hidden shaft (inside the wall)

Map note 17 (GM only) marks the hidden shaft inside the wall.

• ★ Silas's unwashed tonic glass. The residue is frosted and smells of mint. Medicine or alchemist's supplies DC 13 identifies Banshee's Breath.

  • Drips of pond water continue from the servants' stair toward the chapel door (follows C5).

• ★ A muddy print of a buckled boot on one step, and drips of pond water leading down toward the chapel corridor.
  • 8:57: the ghost brushed past Mrs. Crane here; she screamed.

Rows of dark pews face a plain stone altar and three tall candles. Behind the altar, steps drop away into the family crypt, breathing cold.

  • 8:45: a green glow moved past these windows as Quill dressed below (seen by Morwenna from the stable yard).
  • Candle 11: Quill excuses himself "to say a prayer for Silas in the chapel". He is off to light the brazier.
  • Stairs down to the crypt (level change region).

Stuck ladder rung 3: green light flickers in the chapel window.

• Red herring: Morwenna's carriage, packed trunk and a love letter from "R."

Clues here: @UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.1s2HTGToFPs4Ixm0]{C12 A Letter Signed "R."}

People: @UUID[Actor.KQKJNTGmT2yOlb2U]{Lady Morwenna Ravenmoor}

Morwenna spent 8:30-9:00 here loading the carriage.

Epilogue: the real ghost

As you step out into the grey before dawn, Bramwell's warding lanterns around the pond flicker, one by one, from orange to green. On the still water stands a pale woman in a veil, holding a lantern of green glass. She bows her head to you, once. Then the fog closes, and she is gone.

  • Bramwell's warding lanterns and Elspeth's memorial stone.
  • Bramwell spent 8:30-9:00 here lighting the lanterns. Helping him relight them unlocks his testimony.
  • Epilogue: on the memorial stone, the party finds Elspeth's old green-glass lantern, dry and warm. It works as a lantern of revealing.

People: @UUID[Actor.64tWZkvT3Aq5BPNj]{Bramwell Hatch} · @UUID[Actor.6hoDNI4zCBNk0fpK]{The Lantern Widow}

The six warding lanterns are lights labelled 'Warding lantern'; the epilogue macro tints them green.

• ★ Two empty scarecrow posts, their straw scattered toward the chapel.

Clues here: @UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.KlL6idxMjLbYdsBR]{C9 Empty Scarecrow Posts}

One scarecrow still stands on its post. It is just a scarecrow.

The main stair opens onto a long landing hung with a single faded tapestry. One candle burns at the top of the stairs.

  • Doors to Silas's bedchamber and the minstrels' gallery.

A great curtained bed, a velvet robe thrown over a chair, and the smell of liniment. The bed has not been slept in.

  • Silas did not come here after the feast; he went straight to his study at 8:25.

• The bed is still unturned, and the fireplace has been cold all night.
  • ★ An alchemy notebook (Handout 4) with a recipe for Banshee's Breath (Investigation DC 13).
  • A stick of green sealing wax that matches the seal on Edric's debt letter.
  • 8:45: Mrs. Crane found this room dark and empty. At candle 4 Quill claims he was "resting in his room"; it is still dark.

Clues here: ★ @UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.fIUcA6ktUrArCZ7C]{H4 A Page from Quill's Notebook} · @UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.xqgDScd10E4xot3v]{C10 A Stick of Green Wax}

  • An ink-stained witch costume lies crumpled by the bed: she spent 8:30-9:00 changing out of it (true).

Clues here: @UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.CIwbw1l6GjX0G47n]{C13 Pip's Spell Notes}

People: @UUID[Actor.QBfMKJlkNIfQacwd]{Penelope "Pip" Ravenmoor}

The notes' latest entry is a week old. Tonight's ghost was not hers.

Black silk, a vanity swept almost bare, and a faint perfume of violets. The wardrobe stands half empty.

  • Her claimed alibi is "in my room with a headache". The bed is untouched and her trunk is gone (it is in the carriage in the stables).

People: @UUID[Actor.KQKJNTGmT2yOlb2U]{Lady Morwenna Ravenmoor}

Points to her real secret, not to the murder.

• ★ Glowing green smears on the railing. Nature DC 12 identifies foxfire, a glowing fungus paste, not magic.
  • Detect magic shows no magic at all: no illusion, no necromancy. Whatever snuffed the candles was not a spell.
  • 8:55: the Lantern Widow appeared here. By the time anyone reaches the gallery, it is empty.

Clues here: ★ @UUID[JournalEntry.pAwCKlZe6zWlLItH.JournalEntryPage.PDsKGKL6GrJyWOGx]{C4 Glowing Smears}

Reveal the foxfire tile right after the ghost scene.

A plain corridor in the old servants' wing, running past the linen closet to the study and Mrs. Crane's room.

  • Connects the gallery to the study, Mrs. Crane's room, the linen closet and the head of the servants' stair.
  • From Scene 5 on, the study door hangs from one hinge where it was broken in.

If the party posted a guard on the study door in Act 1, it stood here; no one passed it.

Lord Silas Ravenmoor is a thin old man wrapped in a velvet robe, leaning on a raven-headed cane. Behind him, a fire crackles beneath tall bookshelves. On his desk sits a small iron lockbox and a vase of white lilies.

Scene 5: The body (9:00 PM)

Silas sits rigid in his chair, eyes wide, mouth open in a silent scream. Frost glitters on his fingertips. The window hangs open to the night, and wet footprints trail across the rug from the sill to the desk. The lockbox stands open and empty, and its key is gone from Silas's watch chain. White lilies lie scattered across the floor.

  • Scene 2 (7:00 PM), what the party sees while Silas is alive: the window is latched from inside and thick ivy grows undisturbed across the outer sill; the lilies are already on the desk (Mrs. Crane put them there); the lockbox key hangs on Silas's watch chain; one bookcase stands slightly away from the wall (passive Perception 15 notices a cold draft).
  • ★ Poison, not fright: frost on the fingertips and blue-tinged lips in a warm room point to a cold-acting poison (Medicine DC 12).
  • ★ Staged window: the wet footprints run from the sill to the desk but never back, and the ivy outside is undisturbed. The window was opened from inside (Investigation DC 12).
  • ★ The bookcase: a pale scuff arc on the floorboards and a cold draft. Pulling Hallowed Rites of the Ravenmoor Line swings the case open (Investigation DC 14, or passive Perception 15).
  • Missing key: the lockbox key is gone from Silas's watch chain. Whoever opened the box took it, and Quill plants it in Edric's coat at candle 8.
  • Red herring: the scattered lilies (Mrs. Crane's).

A narrow iron bed made with military corners. On the shelf, a pressed white lily lies beside a small portrait of a smiling young woman holding a lantern.

  • The portrait is Elspeth. Supports Mrs. Crane's secret: the lilies are her yearly tribute.

People: @UUID[Actor.bcnzHQSfDwEzt1u1]{Mrs. Agatha Crane}

The top of the steep servants' stair, worn hollow in the middle by forty years of Mrs. Crane.

  • The route Quill took up to the gallery in costume and back down past Mrs. Crane at 8:57 (level change region).

The boot print (C5) is halfway down, on the ground-floor map.
Shelves of folded sheets that smell of lavender. Nothing here but linen, and perhaps a hiding player.

• Edric's empty bottles and the old bricked-up arch. With an ear to the bricks, you can hear water dripping in the crypt beyond.
  • Edric spent 8:30-9:00 here alone, drinking (true). At about 8:40 he heard footsteps and dripping behind the arch.

After the fight, Quill waits here under guard for the dawn constable.

  • ★ Fresh candle wax on the steps, green glowing smudges on the walls, and a dropped sprig of frost-mint.

Joins the study (hidden stair) to the crypt through the secret door behind Elspeth's tomb. The bricked-up arch to the cellar blocks movement but passes sound.

The showdown (midnight)

Green fire roars in the brazier. Dr. Quill stands inside a chalk circle, his beaked mask gleaming, the will held over the flames. "Ravenmoor's dead belong to me tonight." Coffin lids grind open. In the corner, two scarecrows lift their carved pumpkin heads, candlelight blazing behind their grins.

  • ★ The costume: in an empty wall niche behind Elspeth's tomb, a bundle holding a pale gown, a veil, gloves crusted with foxfire paste, a green-glass lantern and a flask of pond water (Investigation DC 13).
  • ★ Moonsilver: a silver-blue glint in a crack in the crypt floor (Arcana or Nature DC 14). Someone has been chipping at it.
  • Two pumpkin-headed scarecrows stand oddly in the corner, and a chalk circle is half-hidden under a tarp. Quill has prepared for trouble; this foreshadows the finale.
  • The Hallows' brazier stands ready to be lit at midnight.
  • Showdown terrain: about 50 by 40 feet, dim light. Stone coffins give half cover. Two iron candelabras can be knocked over (an action) to set a 10-foot square ablaze for 2d6 fire damage to anything inside.

A Page from Quill's Notebook

Banshee's Breath.

Nightshade, frost-mint, powdered ghost orchid. Steep cold. Onset three quarters of an hour. The skin chills and the face sets as if in terror. Mint masks the bitterness. In a tonic, undetectable to the untrained.

Clue C10 · Dr. Quill's room

A Stick of Green Wax

On the writing desk sits a half-used stick of green sealing wax. The bed is still made and the hearth is cold. No one has used this room tonight.

Found in Dr. Quill's guest room

DM: Found: @UUID[JournalEntry.arD2C75cqVJAaZm3.JournalEntryPage.h4oT4q0kwI7dIAMF]{Dr. Quill's Guest Room}. Searching the desk.

Points to: Quill sealed Edric's letter (pairs with H3 on the checklist). Unmasking: why.

Clue C11 · The library

The Old Floor Plan

A yellowed floor plan of Ravenmoor, a century old. A dotted line climbs from the chapel crypt through the walls and ends behind the bookshelves of the master's study. Beside it, in faded ink: Old stair. Cellar arch bricked up.

Found among the family records

DM: Found: @UUID[JournalEntry.arD2C75cqVJAaZm3.JournalEntryPage.kTWLQsu8We2OE6zl]{Library}. Searching the family records.

Checks (speed only, never gate a ★ clue): History DC 13 · Investigation DC 13

Points to: The secret passage (The killer used the passage). Unmasking: how.

Clue C12 · The stables

A Letter Signed "R."

My darling, the carriage will wait at dawn as we agreed. Bring only what you can carry, and leave Ravenmoor and its ghosts behind forever. Every hour until then is an age.

— R.

Found in Lady Morwenna's glove or her carriage

DM: Found: @UUID[JournalEntry.arD2C75cqVJAaZm3.JournalEntryPage.gafL35qf99SPkcCB]{Stables} (@UUID[Actor.KQKJNTGmT2yOlb2U]{Morwenna's glove or the stables}). Searching the carriage, or Morwenna confides.

Points to: Red herring: Morwenna's elopement.

Clue C13 · Pip's room

Pip's Spell Notes

A notebook crammed with spell diagrams. Several pages sketch a veiled woman holding a lantern, with notes: Minor illusion. Light only, no sound. Gallery, after dinner. Make her glow softer. The latest entry is dated a week ago.

Found on Pip's writing desk

DM: Found: @UUID[JournalEntry.arD2C75cqVJAaZm3.JournalEntryPage.OGKS5FPrpbz5sxCZ]{Pip's Room}. Searching the room.

Points to: Red herring: Pip's earlier fake ghosts.

Clue C14 · Dr. Quill's bag

The New Will

I, Silas Ravenmoor, leave Ravenmoor Manor and its grounds to the village of Hollow Brook, as a home for orphaned children. Let the silver beneath the chapel pay for their keep. To my wife, my son, my granddaughter, Mrs. Crane and Mr. Hatch: a stipend each. To whoever unmasks my killer, should it come to that: my cane, and my thanks.

— S. R.

 

Found in the false bottom of the bag

DM: Found: False bottom of Quill's medical bag (@UUID[Actor.ZDkjX7Z2611aYmXT]{False bottom of Quill's medical bag}). Investigation DC 15, or found automatically when Quill is searched after the accusation. Finding it before midnight starts the finale early.

Checks (speed only, never gate a ★ clue): Investigation DC 15 · Sleight of Hand DC 15 (lifting it from the bag)

Points to: The proof, and the ending (The killer is Quill). Unmasking: who, why.

Cards tick themselves when revealed with the Reveal Handout macro. Tick testimony and speak with dead with the Clue Tracker macro.
